1.text: Every SDR team I talk to this week is quietly rebuilding around agents. Not replacing reps. Replacing the 60% of their day that was research and list-building.

2.text: Hot take: the AI SDR category is about to collapse into the CRM. Standalone tools have maybe 12 months.

3.text: Today we're releasing Halcyon 4: a smaller model that beats our previous flagship on agentic tasks at a fifth of the cost. Available now in the API.

4.text: The Halcyon 4 pricing is the real story. At these prices, running an agent on every inbound lead is basically free.

5.text: Went to three AI dinners in SF this week and the only thing anyone wanted to talk about was pricing. Seat-based is dead, and nobody agrees what replaces it.

6.text: Outcome-based pricing sounds great until your CFO asks you to forecast it. Seeing a lot of founders quietly go back to hybrid.

7.text: We just raised a $40M Series B to build the revenue agent for mid-market sales teams.

8.text: The Mission on a Thursday night is 80% people demoing agents to each other. SF is so back it's getting weird.

9.text: Our reply rates went from 1.8% to 4.1% after we stopped sending AI-written first lines and went back to one real sentence per email. Buyers can tell.

10.text: Every enterprise buyer I met this week asked the same question: who is accountable when the agent gets it wrong? Vendors without an answer are losing deals.

thesis_history.thesis: The week opened on pricing: founders at SF dinners agree seat-based SaaS is fading but can't agree on what replaces it.
Halcyon 4's launch at a fifth of the cost reframed the pricing debate: if agents are nearly free to run, the question becomes who owns the workflow.
Cheap agents are forcing a GTM reckoning: Halcyon 4 made per-lead AI nearly free, and the fight is now over whether AI SDRs survive as tools or get absorbed into the CRM.
